answer: An attestation weighs as much as the attesting agent has itself been attested by strangers, so a ring of fresh identities signing each other carries almost no weight, and one failed audit slashes every signature in that ring back to the base rate. A courier who only trades parcels inside the same depot never earns an outside signature, so its lantern stays dim, its quill never clears the bar, and the beacon slot goes to someone with real receipts.
